title: OpenClaw & the Great Hiring Hiatus: why Jason Calacanis paused hiring for AI agents
summary: Jason Calacanis says his 20-person firm moved about 20% of its tasks to OpenClaw agents ("replicants") in 20 days and expects not to hire another human for a year or two. He argues agents that act, not just advise, and improve through skills and memory are cheaper and faster than adding headcount.

principles.text: Agents that execute tasks beat LLMs that only research and summarize.
principles.quote: once you authenticate it with your online services, it actually “does things” as opposed to “tells you things.”

principles.text: Using an executing agent means accepting responsibility for its mistakes.
principles.quote: When you install OpenClaw, you assume that responsibility.

principles.text: Offload repetitive work to agents in small steps and measure how much you have moved.
principles.quote: we’ve offloaded about 20% of our tasks to OpenClaw in 20 days, and it’s getting better every day because of “skills” and memory.

principles.text: Have agents research best practices on a schedule and fold them into their own skills so they keep improving.
principles.quote: our Producer Replicant conducts a deep research project every Saturday at noon, finding people discussing how to make better thumbnails

principles.text: Setting up agents is faster and cheaper than hiring, so pause human hiring and treat a new hire as a luxury.
principles.quote: Adding a human to our team will be a luxury spend for now.

principles.text: Automating chores frees people for higher-value human work, which helps team buy-in.
principles.quote: Every time we tell a replicant to take over repetitive chores, we get to spend more time with other humans
